reference.title: This is not an official price list
reference.body: The figures on this page are collected from reviewed editor submissions and are a market reference only. What a project actually pays depends on many factors and can differ a great deal.
points: Read a typical range, not a fixed number: the median and the middle 50% band (25th–75th percentile) show where most deals land.
A median is only published when at least 3 approved submissions exist; below that you see just the observed range of the samples we have.
The factors that move a price — from runtime to commercial usage rights — are explained further down this page.
No figure here is "the correct price". Agree the scope and delivery terms with the client before you quote.

factors.title: What moves the price
factors.intro: These are the same factors captured in each submission. Two projects of identical length can legitimately land at very different numbers.

items.name: Video duration
items.detail: Longer rushes and timelines mean more time watching, cutting and rendering.

items.name: Complexity
items.detail: A simple narrative with clean cuts versus a fast-paced piece heavy on effects.

items.name: Number of deliverables
items.detail: One master plus cutdowns and a version per platform.

items.name: Motion graphics
items.detail: Titles, animated captions, infographics and logo stings are separate hours.

items.name: Color work
items.detail: A basic balance versus a cinematic look with scopes and a calibrated monitor.

items.name: Sound work
items.detail: Dialogue cleanup, effects, music and the final mix.

items.name: Revision count
items.detail: Define the free-revision boundary in the contract; extra rounds mean extra days.

items.name: Turnaround time
items.detail: A rushed delivery usually adds a significant percentage to the price.

items.name: Commercial usage rights
items.detail: Broadcast, paid ads or corporate usage all push the price up.

items.name: Experience level
items.detail: Junior, mid or senior: experience buys speed, better judgement and less risk.

scenarios.title: Three example scenarios
scenarios.intro: These are built from the data on this page to make comparison easier — they are not price recommendations.

items.title: Instagram reel for a small business
items.summary: A 30–60 second cut from supplied footage, animated captions, one revision round.
items.factors: Short runtime · standard complexity · one deliverable · light motion · normal turnaround · social usage
items.price: Common range in the data: roughly 3–6 million Toman at mid level

items.title: 15-minute YouTube video
items.summary: Narrative edit, dialogue cleanup, music, basic grading and two or three revisions.
items.factors: 15–30 min runtime · standard-to-complex · sound and color work · non-commercial usage
items.price: Common range in the data: roughly 9–13 million Toman at mid level

items.title: 30-second broadcast commercial
items.summary: Fast pace, motion graphics, cinematic grade, sound mix and several cutdowns.
items.factors: Multiple deliverables · many revisions · rush turnaround · broadcast or paid-ad rights
items.price: Common range in the data: from about 40 million Toman (mid) up to 150 million (senior)
